html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Describe the CNCF bodies: Governing Board, TOC, TAGs, TCGs and the end user community
  • Order the maturity levels: sandbox, incubating, graduated, and know archived
  • Explain SIGs, working groups and KEPs in the Kubernetes community
  • Name the next exams after the KCNA

2The CNCF mission, Governing Board, TOC, TAGs and TCGs, the end user community

Running case

Harbor Books Joins the Community

  • The team relies on open source projects from the CNCF landscape, and wants to judge how mature a project is before adopting it
  • One engineer wants to report a bug and propose a small change to Kubernetes
  • A developer asks which exam to take after the KCNA
  • In this module you learn who governs the ecosystem and how to take part

The CNCF and Its Bodies Moving

  • Mission: make cloud native computing ubiquitous, by fostering open source, vendor-neutral projects
  • The Governing Board sets the budget and business direction; the TOC is the technical body that admits, oversees and archives projects
  • TAGs (technical advisory groups) and TCGs (technical community groups) gather experts around topics
  • The end user community speaks for the people who use CNCF projects
  • As of 30 October 2026: five TAGs, such as Security and Compliance, and four TCGs, such as Platform Engineering; earlier TAGs were archived

Exam tip

The board is business, the TOC is technology, end users bring needs.

3Project maturity levels, archived projects, the landscape

Project Maturity and the Landscape Moving

  • Sandbox: experimental, not yet widely tested in production
  • Incubating: used successfully in production by a small number of users, with a healthy pool of contributors
  • Graduated: stable, widely adopted and production ready
  • Archived: the project reached the end of its lifecycle and became inactive
  • The CNCF landscape is a map of cloud native projects and products
  • As of 30 October 2026: 39 projects are graduated, including Kubernetes, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Argo, Flux and Helm

Exam tip

Sandbox, incubating, graduated; archived is the end of the road.

4Kubernetes SIGs, working groups, KEPs, the code of conduct, contributing, the path to the next exams

The Kubernetes Community

Group or term What it is
SIG (Special Interest Group) a persistent, open group that owns a part of the project and its subprojects
Working group a temporary group for an issue that crosses SIG boundaries; it owns no code
Committee chartered for sensitive topics, such as the steering committee or the code of conduct
KEP a Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal: tracks a new feature through alpha, beta and stable
Release Team runs each release cycle
  • Anyone may take part if they follow the Code of Conduct, which Kubernetes takes from the CNCF
  • Principles: open, welcoming, transparent and merit-based
  • Ways to contribute: docs, code, issues and talks; KubeCon + CloudNativeCon is the community conference
Exam tip

SIGs own areas, working groups cross them, KEPs plan features.

From the KCNA to the Next Exams Moving

Exam Format Notes
KCNA multiple choice, 90 minutes no prerequisites; valid for 2 years
KCSA multiple choice, 90 minutes the cloud native security associate exam; no prerequisites
CKA performance-based, in a command line, 2 hours the administrator exam
CKAD performance-based, in a command line the application developer exam
CKS performance-based, in a command line the security specialist exam; you must pass the CKA first
  • As of 30 October 2026: the Linux Foundation suggests the KCSA or the CKA as the next step after the KCNA
Exam tip

KCNA and KCSA are multiple choice; CKA, CKAD and CKS are hands-on.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which CNCF body is the technical governing body that admits and oversees projects?

  • AThe Governing Board, which sets the budget and the business direction of the foundation
  • BThe End User Technical Advisory Board, which speaks for the people who use the projects
  • CA Technical Community Group, which gathers a community around a topic such as platform engineering
  • DThe Technical Oversight Committee, which admits, oversees and archives CNCF projects
Show the answer

Answer: D. The TOC is the CNCF's technical decision body. The Governing Board handles budget and business direction, the End User TAB speaks for users, and TCGs and TAGs are community and advisory groups.

S2Harbor Books wants a project that is stable, widely adopted and production ready. Which CNCF maturity level describes such a project?

  • AGraduated, the level for stable and widely adopted projects
  • BIncubating, the level for projects that a small number of users run in production
  • CSandbox, the level for experimental projects that are not yet widely tested
  • DArchived, the level for projects that reached the end of their lifecycle
Show the answer

Answer: A. Graduated projects are stable, widely adopted and production ready. Incubating projects have a smaller base of production users, sandbox projects are experimental, and archived projects are at the end of their lifecycle.

S3What is the difference between a Kubernetes SIG and a working group?

  • AA SIG is temporary and owns nothing, while a working group is persistent and owns subprojects
  • BA SIG handles the code of conduct, while a working group handles releases
  • CA SIG is persistent and owns part of the project, while a working group is temporary and crosses SIG boundaries
  • DA SIG is chartered for sensitive topics, while a working group may keep its proceedings private
Show the answer

Answer: C. A SIG is a persistent, open group that owns a part of the project and its subprojects. A working group is temporary and addresses issues that cross SIG boundaries, and it owns no code. Committees handle sensitive topics.

6Quick Reference Card
